title: PagerFlow: incident communication templates + response scripts (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a lightweight, transferable kit for run-of-the-mill and high-severity incidents. It is intentionally concise so on-call responders can copy/paste, adapt, and publish quickly. Focus areas: status page snippets, customer-facing bulletins, internal command-center checklist, and short response scripts for initial triage.

How to use this file (quick):
- Immediately after paging: open this doc and pick the severity tier below.
- Publish a status stub within 10 minutes using 'Status page: initial' template.
- Post internal bulletin to #incidents and start the incident bridge (see checklist).
- Use customer template for external-facing accounts (segment by SLA tier).

Severity tiers (use first-match):
- P0 / Emergency: widespread outages, failed model serving, data loss exposure. Publish every 15m until mitigated.
- P1 / Degraded: higher latency or partial feature loss affecting many users. Publish every 30-60m.
- P2 / Performance/Minor: increased latency on non-critical paths, or single-region slowdowns. Publish initial + one follow-up.

Status page templates
1) Status page: initial (copy to status page dashboard)
- Title: Service disruption impacting model inference (region/tier)
- Time: {{ISO_TIMESTAMP}}
- Impact: Customers may experience failed requests or elevated latency for text generation/embeddings in <region>.
- Scope: We have detected increased error rates for some API endpoints; onboarded traffic may be redirected to healthy capacity.
- Current status: Investigating — we have engineers actively looking into the root cause.
- Next update: {{+15m}}
- Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}

2) Status page: mitigation in progress
- Title: Mitigation in progress — degraded performance reduced
- Time: {{ISO_TIMESTAMP}}
- Impact: Error rates are reduced but intermittent failures may occur for a subset of customers in <region>.
- What we're doing: Rolling back recent routing change / scaling extra worker pool / activating fallback model.
- ETA: ~{{ETA}} minutes for stabilization; next update: {{+30m}}

3) Status page: resolved
- Title: Service restored — monitoring
- Time: {{ISO_TIMESTAMP}}
- Impact: All services are operating normally; we will continue monitoring for the next 2 hours.
- Postmortem: A follow-up summary will be posted when available.

Customer-facing templates (pick tone by severity)
- High-severity (P0) external bulletin
Subject: Urgent: temporary outage affecting inference in <region>
Body: Hi <CustomerName>,
We’re reaching out because you may be seeing failed or slow API requests for Redwood Inference in <region>. Our on-call team detected this at {{ISO_TIMESTAMP}} and is actively investigating. We understand this impacts your production traffic and are prioritizing a mitigation.
What we know now: increased error rates originating from <component or cluster> — scope is being assessed.
What we’re doing: scaling extra capacity, enabling fallback routing, and a hotfix is being evaluated.
When we’ll update: next update in 15 minutes, or sooner if we have new information.
Contact: Your account rep is on the incident bridge and will notify you directly if your SLA requires. For urgent escalation reply to this message or contact support@redwood.ai.
Thanks for your patience — we’ll keep you updated.
- Low-tone (P1/P2) customer bulletin
Subject: Degraded performance noticed for inference in <region>
Body: Hi <CustomerName>,
We detected elevated latency for some requests in <region> beginning at {{ISO_TIMESTAMP}}. We don’t expect data loss; root cause is under investigation. We’ll share an update within 60 minutes.

Legal-safe phrasing (for Customer Success/Legal review)
- Avoid speculation: do not use root-cause language until confirmed.
- Commit to monitoring and follow-up: give a specific next-update time window.
- Offer contact path: include account rep or premium support escalation.

Internal command-center (incident bridge) checklist — rapid sequence
1) Kickoff (first 5 min)
- Assign INCIDENT_LEAD (owner for the bridge) and COMM_LEAD (owns status page & external messages).
- Set bridge link and Slack channel: create thread in #incidents and pin link to bridge.
- Post INITIAL internal bulletin (use 'internal bulletin' template below).
- Attach key telemetry: SLO dashboards, recent deploys, autoscaler logs, error spike graphs.

2) Triage (5–20 min)
- Quick hypothesis grid: network | model runtime | routing | recent deploys | infra autoscaling | storage.
- Check recent merges and deploys: run git log + last deploy IDs (Jenkins/GH Actions).
- Confirm if mitigation is needed: increase replicas, toggle fallback model, or roll back recent deploy.

3) Mitigation (20–60 min)
- Apply mitigation with a single commited actor (assignee) and verify metrics within 5–10 min.
- If mitigation works: update status page to 'mitigation in progress' and CRITICAL customers via direct message.
- If mitigation fails: escalate to SRE lead and consider failover to alternate region.

4) Stabilize & close (after service normal)
- Set status page to 'resolved' and prepare postmortem notes.
- Run blast radius review: list impacted customers and affected features.
- Start postmortem owner assignment and timeline for a full RCA within 72 hours.

Internal bulletin (copy into #incidents)
- Subject: [INCIDENT_ID] Investigating elevated errors — <service/component>
- Body: Timeline: first alarm at {{ISO_TIMESTAMP}}.
Short summary: Elevated 5xx/error-rate for <endpoint>.
Initial actions: scaling + rollback candidate identified + triage team assigned.
Bridge: {{BRIDGE_LINK}} | Comm lead: @<handle> | Incident lead: @<handle>

Response scripts (quick paste for engineers)
- When asked to check logs: 'Run: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=worker --since=10m | grep ERROR'
- To inspect replication: 'kubectl get hpa,pods -n inference -o wide'
- To trigger fallback routing: 'rlsctl route set inference --fallback=true --force' (OPS-only)
- Hot rollback (when authorized): 'deployctl rollback inference-deployment --to=previous --confirm'

Escalation triggers (suggested)
- Fail open: auto-retry > 20% of inbound requests for > 10 minutes -> escalate to P0.
- Latency: p95 > 2s for > 15 minutes for production tier -> escalate to P1.
- Data integrity: any sign of dropped or corrupted user data -> immediate P0 + legal & security on-call.

Post-incident checklist (first 72h)
- Capture full timeline and raw artifacts (logs, traces, deploy ids) and attach to Jira ticket.
- Run smoke tests against canary and prod after mitigation.
- Draft customer-facing root cause summary (with COMM_LEAD).
- Schedule RCA with relevant owners inside 48–72h; assign action items with due dates.

Open questions / TODOs (for this draft)
- Standardize exact SLA wording for Status page vs. direct customer messages.
- Add quick links to observability dashboards (Grafana/Tempo) for each service.
- Make checklist one-click in our incident tooling (nice-to-have).

Notes to on-call (short):
- Publish early, publish often. Even "we're still investigating" helps reduce duplicate pages.
- Keep copy simple and factual. Avoid root-cause claims until validated.
- Use templates and fill placeholders — speed beats prose in the first 30 minutes.

Example filled initial status (for quick copy/paste):
- Title: Service disruption impacting inference (us-west1)
- Time: 2025-07-12T14:03:00Z
- Impact: Some customers in us-west1 may experience 500 errors for text generation endpoints.
- Status: Investigating
- Incident ID: RF-2025-0712-01
- Next update: 2025-07-12T14:18:00Z

Revision history:
- 2024-11-03: initial draft by Aisha P.
- 2025-02-17: updated escalation triggers and response scripts (Miguel S.)
- 2025-08-12: added legal-safe phrasing and customer escalation notes (Rina K.)

End of draft — feedback welcome in thread.
